To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the five tumour markers studied have no value in the screening of breast cancer patients, in the differential diagnosis between breast cancer and benign disease or in the prediction of response to treatment.
serum CEA and erythrocytes sedimentation rate (esr) are the most reliable tumour markers in the management of systemic breast cancer.

the five tumour markers we studied were not significantly elevated in patients with primary breast cancer, but were significantly elevated in patients who subsequently developed systemic disease, and sequential changes in serum C-reactive protein and carcinoembry-onic antigen levels correlated with response to therapy in this group of patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of serum tumour markers to assess the response to therapy in breast cancer.
the use of serum markers to assess response to treatment of breast cancer.
the role of five serum tumour markers (CEA, ferritin, orsosomucoid, C-reactive protein, ESR) in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the five serum markers studied have no role in the early diagnosis of breast cancer, nor are they useful in the differential diagnosis between benign and malignant breast disease.
the serum levels of CEA and ERS are of value for the assessment of response of breast cancer to treatment, but are not useful in the diagnosis of breast cancer.
CEA and ESD are the only tumour markers of value for monitoring systemic breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CEA, ferritin, orsosomucoid, CRP and ESR are not useful for the screening of breast cancer.
the five markers are not useful as screening tests or in the differentialdiagnosis of breast cancer but they are useful in the assessment of the response of patients with systemic disease.
the serum CEA and erythrocytes sedimentation rate are the best markers of response in systemic breast cancer and should be used routinely for the assessment of treatment response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown for the first time the importance of using a combination of tumour markers in the diagnosis and management of breast cancer.
CEA and ERS are the only markers that correlate significantly with the response to therapy and therefore may be used in the assessment of the response in patients with systemic cancer.
the five tumor markers are not helpful for screening, early detection, or differential diagnosis of breast cancers.
